- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment history more heavily in final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows a sudden shift from negative to positive, model often misses the reversal; add a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast.
- When true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ days), model may be overfitting recent highs; apply a 10–15% downward bias for next 3–5 days.
